items.name: Dev
items.desc: In the classical epic poetry, fairy tales (masals), and oral mythologies of Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and the wider Central Asian region, the Dev (or Div) is a formidable, giant-like mythical being associated with subterranean caverns, towering mountains, and hidden treasures. Derived from ancient Indo-Iranian and Turkic mythological roots, Devs are typically depicted as gigantic, anthropomorphic creatures of immense physical strength, often possessing multiple heads or horns, and living in remote mountain fortresses or underground palaces. In traditional tales, while some Devs serve as terrifying antagonists guarding enchanted princesses or subterranean hoards, others can be cunningly outwitted or bound by magical talismans by clever heroes.

items.name: The Universal Basilisk
items.desc: A legendary serpent or dragon, the Basilisk is known as the king of serpents, with a gaze and breath so venomous it can kill anything it encounters.

items.name: Ciguapa
items.desc: In the vibrant and mysterious folklore of the Dominican Republic and the wider Caribbean, the Ciguapa is a legendary, elusive female creature said to inhabit the deep, mountainous tropical forests and caves of the island. According to traditional Dominican oral narratives, the Ciguapa possesses an arresting and unusual physical feature: her feet face backward, causing her footprints to point in the opposite direction of where she is actually heading, successfully confounding any hunters or travelers attempting to track her. Described as possessing wild, cascading dark hair that covers her entire body like a garment, the Ciguapa roams the moonlit jungle canopy at night, feeding on raw fruit, tender leaves, and occasionally visiting rural farms.
